# Prague Metro — Growth Through Time

> An interactive, single-page map of how the Prague Metro grew: every line extension, station
> rename and closure from opening day (9 May 1974) to today, plus Line D under construction.
> Pick any date and see that day's network with that day's station names. Free, no account,
> no ads, no cookies. English, with a short Czech summary.

## What it is
- A history visualisation, not a journey planner. Scrub the timeline or press Play to watch
  the network grow; tap a station for its opening date and former name.
- Six small maps (1974, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, today) show the whole history at a glance;
  each moves the main map to that date. The slider's track is a chart of stations open.
- Lines A (green), B (yellow), C (red) as built; Line D in its official blue, dashed where
  under construction, dotted where only planned.
- Below the map: a table of every opening, the complete 1990 rename list, and Line D status,
  readable without JavaScript.

## Facts (as shown in the app, checked 27 Oct 2026)
- Opened 9 May 1974: line C, 9 stations, Florenc – Kačerov. Line A opened 12 Aug 1978, line B
  2 Nov 1985.
- Today: 58 stations on lines A, B, C; interchanges Muzeum (A/C), Můstek (A/B), Florenc (B/C).
  Latest opening: line A west to Nemocnice Motol, 6 Apr 2015.
- Renamed 22 Feb 1990 (12 stations): Leninova → Dejvická, Dukelská → Nové Butovice,
  Švermova → Jinonice, Moskevská → Anděl, Sokolovská → Florenc, Fučíkova → Nádraží
  Holešovice, Gottwaldova → Vyšehrad, Mládežnická → Pankrác, Primátora Vacka → Roztyly,
  Budovatelů → Chodov, Družby → Opatov, Kosmonautů → Háje.
- Floods: August 2002 (19 stations flooded, sections closed for months); June 2013.
- Line D: Pankrác, Ryšánka, Nádraží Krč, Nemocnice Krč, Nové Dvory, Libuš, Písnice, Depo
  Písnice (plus a planned leg north to Náměstí Míru). Construction began 21 Apr 2022
  (Pankrác – Ryšánka) and June 2026 (Ryšánka – Nové Dvory). DPP expects Pankrác – Nové
  Dvory to open in the second half of 2032.

## Data & provenance
- Dates come from Dopravní podnik hl. m. Prahy (DPP) history pages and press releases and
  Wikipedia's line and station articles. The dataset is embedded in the page and versioned
  in the repository; tests hold the page's text to the map's data. Line D dates are DPP's
  current plan and can slip.
